stories.headline: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang after Trump intervention as US blacklists Megaspeed

sources.body: Nvidia on Monday reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive in a stunning reversal that President Donald Trump said followed his own direct contacts with the company's board. Huang resigned two weeks ago over an affair with a woman whom US intelligence agencies suspect of spying for China, a departure that sent Wall Street tumbling and stoked fears for a US economy reliant on the AI investment boom. FRANCE 24's Carys Garland and Wassim Cornet report.
sources.headline: Nvidia reinstates Huang as CEO after Trump intervention

sources.body:
Bureau of Security and Industry adds Singapore-based firm involved in Nvidia spy scandal to export control list.

The United States has added the Singapore-based company at the centre of an alleged spying scandal involving Nvidia to its trade blacklist.

The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) placed Megaspeed International and six other firms in Southeast Asia on its Entity List on Monday, hours after Jensen Huang returned to Nvidia as CEO in a stunning comeback that sent tech stocks soaring.

Megaspeed and the other entities were determined to be “acting contrary to the national security or foreign policy interests of the United States”, BIS, which sits under the US Department of Commerce, said in a filing to the Federal Register.

The designations mean that anyone seeking to ship the entities advanced US technology, including Nvidia’s top-end graphics processing units (GPUs) used in AI, must obtain an export licence.

Megaspeed’s blacklisting comes as divisions in US President Donald Trump’s administration over China’s access to Nvidia chips have been laid bare in recent weeks amid claims Huang was romantically involved with a woman accused of working with Chinese intelligence.

While US officials have been scrutinising Megaspeed’s compliance with export controls for years, US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick’s department had declined to place the company on its trade blacklist, prompting recriminations from administration officials known to hold more hawkish views on China, including Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent.

Trump on Monday played down the national security concerns around Nvidia as he confirmed that he had personally intervened with the company’s board of directors to push for Huang’s reinstatement.

Trump, who has cultivated a close relationship with the top Nvidia executive during his second term, told CNBC that he felt “very strongly” about Huang’s role at the chip giant and that he offered the board assurances about risks to national security.

Shaoyu Yuan, a visiting assistant professor at New York University’s Center for Global Affairs who specialises in security issues, said Trump’s intervention was the latest example of the president making policy based on personal rapport rather than a “consistent security standard”.

“The incoherence is in the wider policy. Washington blacklists a middleman for moving Nvidia chips to China while it licenses Nvidia to sell H200 chips to China directly and takes a 25 percent cut,” Yuan told Al Jazeera, referring to the Trump administration’s announcement last year that it would allow the sale of some Nvidia GPUs to China in exchange for the company handing over a portion of the revenues to the government.

“Treasury Secretary Bessent has said other departments wanted this listing for months, and Commerce acted only after the scandal became public.”

US officials have accused Megaspeed International’s former top executive Alice Huang of working with China’s Ministry of State Security in an intelligence-gathering operation targeting Huang.
sources.headline: US adds Megaspeed to trade blacklist as Nvidia’s Huang returns as CEO

sources.body:
Nvidia's market value rose by nearly $1 trillion as its share price skyrocketed after the tech firm reinstated Jensen Huang as its chief executive with immediate effect.

His shock reinstatement comes less than two weeks after Huang resigned after admitting an affair with a woman who was alleged to be a Chinese spy, a period in which shares in the chipmaker have also fallen significantly.

Nvidia shares rose by more than 31% which also lifted stock markets, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq climbing by 6.5% and the S&P 500 also rose 4.75%.

Tech stocks more broadly have also rallied following large falls on Friday , with much of the rally starting in pre-market trading before Huang's return was announced.

Other chipmakers experienced large increases following Monday's announcement from the Nvidia board. Shares in Micron Technology jumped 19%, while AMD shares rose nearly 7%.

Tesla shares also lept up by nearly 11.5%, while other tech gains were more muted by comparison: Amazon shares were up nearly 3.5%, and Apple and Microsoft rose by less than 2%.

While the surge in Nvidia shares was large and drove its market value back towards $4tn, the firm's share price remains about 21% down from a month ago.

A sharp drop occurred on 4 November, after the Democrat's midterm election victory sparked fears of tougher AI regulation to come led to a broad tech stock sell-off.

On Friday alone, Nvidia shares fell by 13.7% as tech stocks more broadly fell, and as Reuters reported - unconfirmed by the BBC - that the company was being investigated by the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) over its accounting practices.

Nvidia is a key firm at the core of the artificial intelligence (AI) boom, with the chips it makes central to the industry.

Nvidia's board of directors voted unanimously to reinstate the firm's co-founder following "a series of discussions and meetings" with him, the company said - but US President Donald Trump has claimed he "convinced" the board to reinstate Huang.

Kathleen Brooks, research director at brokerage firm XTB, said Huang's return showed Huang was the "godfather" of AI, and "has a talismanic influence over the sector".

"Barely two weeks ago this man was ousted from the company that he founded due to serious misconduct and potential national security issues," she said.

"Even though Huang did not hold special voting shares on the board, Nvidia's directors cannot see a future for the company without him."

Dan Coatsworth, head of markets at AJ Bell, said Huang's reinstatement was an astonishing about-turn for Nvidia, particularly given reports of an as-yet unconfirmed SEC investigation.

"This is the biggest corporate U-turn in living memory. To go from being embroiled in a spy scandal to being reinstated as the head of one of the world's most valuable companies in less than a fortnight is nothing short of remarkable," he said.

"Today's stock market rebound represents a massive sigh of relief by investors. However, one cannot rule out a more conservative approach by Huang going forward.
sources.headline: Nvidia value climbs by almost $1tn and tech stocks rally after Jensen Huang returns

stories.headline: NATO pledges space defense amid reports Russia is preparing a nuclear-armed satellite

sources.body:
Nato chief Mark Rutte has said the alliance will defend against any threats in space after reports that Russia was preparing to launch a nuclear-armed satellite.

Intelligence reports about a possible launch in the next 60 days had been shared among Nato countries this month, according to German media outlets. It was not clear which country had authored the reports.

Asked about the reports, Rutte said: "We will always make sure we defend every inch of Nato territory, and that includes making sure we are safe when it comes to the space element."

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said he hadn't seen the latest reports but dismissed reports citing "unknown sources" as "hardly worth taking seriously".

The Russian embassy in Berlin told German media it rejected what it called "unfounded allegations" and said the reports were part of a "propaganda campaign".

Rutte told the press conference in Berlin that Nato had a variety of response options.

"When it comes to the military domain, we will always make assessments of our deterrence and defence and make updates where necessary," he said.

Citing anonymous German military and intelligence sources, the reports by broadcasters NDR and WDR, and newspaper Sueddeutsche Zeitung, said the Russian satellite was dubbed "Sputnik-S" and was equipped with a nuclear warhead. It could be used to disrupt or destroy other satellites, including important communication and observation satellites.

Standing alongside Rutte, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz did not confirm or deny the reports of Russia's plans, but said they "reveal the level of escalation Russia is evidently prepared to pursue".

"Reports that Russia is planning to introduce nuclear weaponry into space are not new, yet they remain no less shocking," he said.

A German government spokesman earlier also did not confirm or deny the reports, but said it was taking the reports "very seriously", AFP reported. The spokesman, however, warned against causing "excessive nervousness regarding hypothetical dangers".

Josef Aschbacher, the head of the European Space Agency, said having nuclear weapons in space was "the ultimate nightmare scenario", German paper Handelsblatt reported.

Russia is a signatory to the 1967 Outer Space Treaty, which bans weapons of mass destruction from orbit. Other countries, including the US and China, have deployed or plan to deploy other weapons in space, exploring other capabilities outside of the treaty, such as targeting rivals' satellites - which are key for military communications, surveillance and navigation.

In 2024 the US claimed Russia was developing a "space-based" anti-satellite weapon armed with a nuclear warhead. Russia denied the accusation .

"Our position is clear and transparent. We have always been categorically against the deployment of nuclear weapons in space and we are still against it," President Vladimir Putin said at the time.

In September the US Secretary of the Air Force Troy Meink said the US had "on-orbit, space-control weapons" circling the planet, but did not provide specifics. In response to the announcement, the Kremlin's Peskov told Russian media that space "must be free of any weapon".
sources.headline: Nato chief vows defence against space threat after Russian nuclear satellite reports

sources.body: NATO chief Mark Rutte said Monday the alliance would defend against threats in space when asked about German media reports that Russia may be preparing to launch a nuclear-armed satellite. The media reports, citing unnamed German military and BND spy agency sources, said Moscow was thought to be planning such a launch in the coming weeks, giving it the capability to destroy other satellites. FRANCE 24's Laurent Berstecher reports.
sources.headline: NATO vows space defence after Russia nuclear satellite report

stories.headline: Ukraine confirms naval drone strikes on two Russian ships off Libya

sources.body:
Ukraine’s security service says seven drones were launched from mothership in operation that sank Merkury warship

Ukraine has confirmed it deployed naval drones in strikes on two Russian vessels off Libya on Sunday, including one that sank the corvette Merkury, one of Russia’s newest vessels.

Ukraine’s security service, the SBU, said seven domestically made naval drones were launched from a mothership in the operation, which Volodymyr Zelenskyy described as “exemplary”.

“We continue our operations in designated waters. We are responding to Russia’s aggression. We are developing Ukrainian weapons,” the Ukrainian president added.

Zelenskyy released video footage, filmed by an approaching drone, showing the drones as they smashed into the side of the warship at its berth in the Benghazi naval base, triggering huge explosions that lit up the night sky.

In its own statement, the SBU said: “The defence forces of Ukraine have once again demonstrated that the Russian military fleet and its logistics networks have no safe routes, even far beyond the Black Sea.”

Zelenskyy said the other vessel hit on Sunday, the dry cargo ship MV Angara, was being used by Russia to transport weapons.

The operation, conducted 1,500 miles (2,400km) from the frontline in Ukraine, was the latest daring long-range assault by Kyiv’s forces. Last week Ukraine hit the Kerch bridge – a key supply line to Russian-occupied Crimea – and the Russian Baltic seaport of Kaliningrad.

Residents in Benghazi heard loud explosions and saw flames at the naval base early on Sunday. Civil defence units rushed to the site and extinguished the fire, authorities in eastern Libya said.

The Institute for the Study of War said the Merkury had stopped over for several days, under a cooperation agreement, to refuel and resupply as it escorted Russian cargo ships that could carry military supplies en route to Russia.

The Merkury had docked to refuel and take on supplies as part of a cooperation agreement between Russia and the eastern-based government in Libya, the statement said without providing details about the vessel or its cargo.

Vladimir Putin had taken a personal interest in the ship. In 2019 he toured the St Petersburg yard where it was being built and backed naming it after a tsarist-era brig celebrated for fighting off two Turkish warships in the Black Sea in 1829.

At the 2023 Navy Day parade, the Russian president singled it out among 30 new vessels as evidence that Russia was “consistently building up the power of its fleet”. He hailed its St George flag as “a sign of the inviolability of our naval traditions” and said it was “gratifying” that the brig’s name had been revived.

Russian state media also talked up the ship. The news agency Tass called it the “newest missile corvette”, while the channel TV Tsentr claimed its stealth technology made it “invisible to radar”.

Divided Libya has emerged in recent years as a proxy battlefield. Moscow has long supported the breakaway government in Benghazi of Khalifa Haftar in its efforts to use eastern Libya as a staging post for its military presence in north Africa and the Sahel.
sources.headline: Ukraine confirms it used naval drones to strike two Russian ships off Libya

sources.body: Authorities in divided Libya's east called on Monday for the United Nations to investigate claims that Ukrainian forces were present in the country's west, as they lodged a complaint over Ukrainian attacks on two Russian ships off Benghazi. The strikes on Sunday, claimed by Kyiv, come as Ukraine steps up strikes against Russia far from the front lines of their war. FRANCE 24's Emerald Maxwell reports.
sources.headline: Libya's east seeks UN probe into claims Ukrainian military present in west

stories.headline: UK sanctions Myanmar military leaders as 14 countries acknowledge Rohingya genocide ruling

sources.body:
The UK has sanctioned five senior Myanmar military leaders after the International Court of Justice (ICJ) ruled that the country had carried out genocide against the Rohingya minority – marking the first time a state has been found guilty of the crime .

A military crackdown in 2017 killed thousands of Rohingya and forced more than 700,000 to flee Buddhist-majority Myanmar, formerly known as Burma.

The UK is joined by several other countries in acknowledging the ICJ ruling, including Australia, Belgium, Portugal, Spain and Canada.

Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said: "Our response to a crime as profoundly shocking as genocide must reflect our values and must be matched by clear action."

The senior military leaders facing sanctions are Myo Htut Hlaing, Myo Min Tun, Myat Thet Oo, Kyaw Soe and Kyaw Swar Oo.

Miliband added that Myanmar's President Min Aung Hlaing , who was sanctioned by the UK in 2021, is "directly responsible for many of the atrocities that have happened" as he was head of the military at the time of the genocide in 2017.

He said: "Myanmar must stop ongoing violations, investigate, prosecute and punish perpetrators, and prevent such an atrocity from ever happening again."

Miliband also called for an "immediate pause in hostilities to enable humanitarian aid to get through, a stop to air strikes on civilians, and the release of political prisoners, as well as dialogue towards an inclusive political settlement".

The foreign secretary confirmed that new legislation would be passed to stop the supply of aviation fuel to the country, which was known as Burma until 1989.

Last week, he expelled Myanmar's defence attaché after the ICJ ruled the country had committed genocide during the brutal military campaign in 2017.

He told MPs on Monday the UK would raise the issue at the UN Security Council this week, and there would be a dedicated meeting in a fortnight.

The court found on Thursday that "genocidal intent is the only reasonable inference that can be drawn from the evidence" it had seen.

The verdict was reached by a majority of nine votes to six among a panel of judges from around the world. The ICJ also found in favour by majority that Myanmar had violated several other parts of the 1948 Genocide Convention .

In its ruling last week, the court determined that about 10,000 Rohingya were murdered during the clearance operation in the western Rakhine state that borders Bangladesh and the Bay of Bengal. Myanmar denied the claims against it.

Reports said that entire villages were burnt down, and that women and girls were raped.

Miliband said more than 1.2 million refugees fled and were being supported by Bangladesh.

Myanmar's leader during the genocide, Aung San Suu Kyi , was deposed by the military in 2021.

MPs heard that air strikes and violence from the Arakan army were still happening.
sources.headline: UK sanctions top Myanmar military leaders after Rohingya genocide ruling

sources.body: 14 from Europe, Africa and Oceania have acknowledged a landmark ruling by the International Court of Justice that Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya minority, calling on the country to comply with its obligations under international law. The United Kingdom separately announced sanctions against five senior Myanmar military figures and said it would formally recognise the genocide.
sources.headline: 14 countries acknowledge ICJ ruling of genocide against Rohingya

stories.headline: Oxfam report finds Gaza's destruction has created a toxic wasteland

sources.body:
Gaza has been turned into "a toxic wasteland", with more than 99% of the Palestinian territory showing indicators of environmental contamination from Israeli military attacks, a new report from the charity Oxfam says .

Heavy metals, explosive residues, asbestos from destroyed buildings, and dioxins and biological contaminants are threats to Palestinians now and potentially for decades to come, it says.

Oxfam International's executive director, Amitabh Behar, said the impact on Gaza "will have fundamentally degraded the environmental conditions necessary for human safety and survival".

In response, the Israeli embassy in the UK said the report "falls short of professional standards".

Behar also accused Israel of "environmental war crimes" as part of an "ongoing genocide in Gaza".

Israel has rejected genocide accusations in an ongoing case at the International Court of Justice as baseless and distorted. It maintains that its military campaign in Gaza is an act of self-defence against Hamas in response to the group's deadly attack on Israel on 7 October 2023, and that it takes steps to mitigate civilian harm.

Oxfam and the UK-based Conflict and Environment Observatory (CEOBS) used satellite imagery, remote sensing, spatial analysis and other open-source data to draw their conclusions in the most comprehensive report to date on the severe environmental impacts caused by three years of intense war in Gaza.

The report details how munitions used in Israel's intense bombardment, as well as the debris from destroyed buildings and infrastructure, all have an impact on the environment. In February, a UN special rapporteur stated that more than 200,000 tonnes of explosives were dropped on Gaza in almost two years - "the equivalent of the total energy of approximately 13 Hiroshima-type nuclear bombs".

Last year, the UN Environment Programme (UNEP) estimated that Israel's military operations destroying homes and infrastructure had generated more than 61 million tonnes of debris across the territory, with about 15% potentially carrying a high risk of contamination from hazardous materials.

"There are going to be chronic health impacts that are long term because a lot of these contaminants are persistent in the environment," Oxfam report author Lama Abdul Samad told the BBC.

She says that now and in future Gazans are likely to suffer from increased respiratory diseases, cancers, organ damage and a rise in birth defects and stillbirths.

With all six wastewater treatment plants out of operation in Gaza, untreated sewage currently makes its way into groundwater and the Mediterranean Sea. The health impact has recently been exacerbated by heavy winter storms causing rainwater to mix with wastewater and flow through streets and tent sites housing displaced people.

Testing types and levels of contamination is often not possible because Gazan laboratories have been destroyed and there are Israeli restrictions on the entry of specialist testing equipment and scientists. The BBC has approached the Israeli military for comment.
sources.headline: Israeli attacks have turned Gaza into 'toxic wasteland', Oxfam says

sources.body:
Scientific and satellite findings warn of widespread contamination in Gaza, posing grave threats to public health ‘for generations to come’

Israel’s destruction of Gaza has left a devastating environmental legacy with poisoned water, contaminated soil and toxic air threatening the life-support systems that the population depends on for survival, according to a report.

Israel’s military assault has created widespread contamination across the entire strip, the report by Oxfam and the Conflict and Environment Observatory (Ceobs) finds, with heavy metals, explosive residues, asbestos from destroyed buildings, and sewage making the air, soil and water dangerous for Palestinians for decades to come.

Oxfam International’s executive director, Amitabh Behar, said: “Israel’s ongoing genocide in Gaza includes military assaults on its environment, which are environmental war crimes threatening life now and for generations to come.”

He said the “destruction and contamination of Gaza” have “fundamentally degraded the environmental conditions necessary for human safety and survival” and breach Israel’s legal obligations under international humanitarian and human rights law.

“Palestinians living in Gaza are being exposed to toxins … through air, food, water and via direct contact with contaminated soils and debris. These risks will persist for generations to come, unless clean-up, remediation and recovery actions are prioritised.”

In 2025 and earlier this year, the UN independent international commission of inquiry found that Israel had committed genocide in Gaza and that Israeli officials, including the prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, incited these acts. The Israeli mission in Geneva said Israel rejected the commission’s “libellous sham”. Netanyahu is separately wanted by the international criminal court (ICC) for war crimes.

Oxfam’s report gives the most comprehensive picture to date of what it calls the “toxic wasteland” created by the Israeli assault which has killed more than 74,000 Palestinians and wounded at least 175,000, while thousands still remain unaccounted for under the rubble.

Using satellite imagery, remote sensing, scientific analysis and other open-source data, it concludes contamination in Gaza is “widespread, severe and consequential, with serious implications for public health and civilian survival”.

Behar said: “It is horrifying to begin to understand the extent of toxic contamination being faced by the population, who can neither escape nor protect themselves properly from the dangers. In an area as small, oppressed and densely populated as Gaza, continuous exposure is inevitable, with people surrounded by waste and sewage, spreading pests and the risk of disease growing.

“Raw sewage is pouring into the sea and leaking into the ground, while the destruction of Gaza’s sanitation systems leaves people with little protection from the contamination around them.”

He added the “associated health consequences will be severe, with children and pregnant women among those facing the highest risks”.
sources.headline: Israel’s destruction of Gaza has created a ‘toxic wasteland’, experts find

stories.headline: Justice Department admits Trump administration deported a US citizen to Mexico

sources.body:
Brian Morales García of Texas seeks damages after he was wrongly identified as undocumented in case White House wants dropped

The Trump administration recently admitted in federal court that it deported a US citizen to Mexico after American authorities incorrectly concluded he was an undocumented immigrant.

Attorneys for the US justice department made that admission on Friday while requesting the dismissal of a lawsuit for damages that the deported man – Brian José Morales García of Austin, Texas – has been pursuing against the federal government.

Morales García’s case took that turn as the White House has faced bipartisan criticism for the aggressive mass deportation campaign pursued by Donald Trump throughout his second presidency – widely seen as a factor in the electoral battering his Republican party suffered during the 3 November midterms, costing it control of Congress .

The Denver-born, Mexico-raised Morales García was riding with his boss to his job as an air-conditioning installation technician on 3 April when they were pulled over by state and local officers near Fredericksburg, Texas.

Morales García was his boss’s passenger and did not have his identification on him. The 25-year-old also told the officers that he had his birth certificate and social security card at home, but they didn’t believe him – so they called immigration agents, who detained Morales García.

Court filings recount how Robert Gil Jr, a US Customs and Border Protection agent, consulted records from Mexico that listed a Mexican birthplace for Morales García. Gil Jr also accused Morales García of saying he was born in Mexico and observed that he only spoke in Spanish, according to court records.

Morales García was deported on 7 April, with the Trump administration later accusing him in a media statement of being in the country illegally.

Morales García’s attorneys sued on 1 May, maintaining that he had falsely said he entered the US illegally and signed papers for a rapid deportation in response to threats of imprisonment by agents. His lawsuit, which seeks an unspecified amount of money, also contended that family and friends tried to deliver documents proving his US citizenship before this deportation.

But those efforts were unduly rebuffed, Morales García’s lawsuit said.

The Trump administration denied Morales García’s assertions, saying on Friday that he went to Mexico voluntarily and therefore lacked any basis to sue the federal government for damages. Nonetheless, in court filings on Friday, the administration conceded that Morales García “was permitted entry” back into the US on 30 August after it reviewed “information concerning plaintiff’s place of birth”.

“Plaintiff is a dual citizen of the United States and Mexico,” Justin Simmons, the US attorney for the western district of Texas, wrote in a court filing first reported by the Texas Tribune .

Americans are not required to carry proof of citizenship when going about their daily business. Lawyers across the US have seen cases such as Morales García’s, which begin after an encounter with local authorities demonstrate how those officials are generally not aware of the nuances of immigration policy.
sources.headline: Trump administration deported US citizen to Mexico, DoJ admits in court

stories.headline: Final election polls diverge sharply: most favor a PP–Vox majority, while CIS puts PSOE ahead

sources.body: <p>Diez días de campaña no parecen haber movido, por ahora, casi nada sustancial en las intenciones de voto para el próximo 29-N, a tenor de la última encuesta de 40dB. para EL PAÍS y la SER antes de que entre en vigor la prohibición legal de publicar sondeos. La sólida ventaja con que <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-11-13/la-campana-arranca-con-la-derecha-en-el-horizonte-de-los-190-escanos.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-11-13/la-campana-arranca-con-la-derecha-en-el-horizonte-de-los-190-escanos.html">el bloque de la derecha inició la carrera electoral</a> apenas ha sufrido una leve erosión. En esta última entrega, la suma de PP, Vox y UPN aparece un poco por debajo de los 190 escaños que se le adjudicaban al comienzo, pero aún con más de 10 de margen sobre la mayoría absoluta del Congreso. <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-11-22/el-psoe-acaricia-el-empate-con-el-pp-segun-el-tracking-de-40db.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-11-22/el-psoe-acaricia-el-empate-con-el-pp-segun-el-tracking-de-40db.html">Sí se ha estrechado la pugna entre PP y PSOE por el primer puesto, </a>pero siempre con los populares por delante tras haber disminuido una parte de sus grandes fugas a Vox.</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-11-23/la-ventaja-de-la-derecha-no-cede-mientras-el-psoe-pugna-por-el-primer-puesto.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>
sources.headline: La ventaja de la derecha no cede mientras el PSOE pugna por el primer puesto

sources.body:
Los candidatos Pedro Sánchez (PSOE), Alberto Núñez Feijóo (PP), Santiago Abascal (Vox) y Ada Colau (Frente Amplio), en diferentes actos electorales de la campaña del 29N. EUROPA PRESS / EFE

En el día en que termina el plazo legal para publicar encuestas, y a seis días de la cita con las urnas, el CIS estima que el PSOE sería el partido más votado si se celebrasen hoy las elecciones generales, con un 34,4% de los votos, casi diez puntos por delante del PP (24,7%) , con Vox en tercer lugar (15,6%) y Frente Amplio en cuarta posición, con un 5,7%. La suma de PP y Vox se quedaría en el 40,3% del apoyo, lejos de las estimaciones de la mayoría de las encuestas.

En cambio, el PSOE y otras formaciones de izquierda (Compromís:Front Valencià, 1,8%; Adelante Andalucía, 1,8%; Podemos, 0,8%; Unidad del Pueblo Canario, 0,4%; y Aramés-Front Ampli, 0,3%) se irían en conjunto al 44,3%, sin contar el potencial apoyo de ERC, EH Bildu o BNG a una eventual investidura de Pedro Sánchez. De nuevo, la estimación del CIS va en sentido contrario al resto de principales sondeos en España.

Es la estimación electoral del barómetro de noviembre (ver en pdf) que publica el Centro de Investigaciones Sociológicas, y que sigue la senda de la macroencuesta electoral que la institución presidida por José Félix Tezanos difundió la víspera de iniciarse la campaña, el 12 de noviembre.

Entonces, también apuntaba que el PSOE sería la fuerza más votada en las elecciones generales del 29 de noviembre con un 33,3% de los votos, que le reportarían entre 134 y 143 escaños , con una ventaja de casi ocho puntos respecto al PP (25,5% del voto y 98-106 escaños), una ventaja que ahora se habría ampliado casi otros dos puntos en apenas diez días, ya que el PSOE sube 1,1 y el PP baja 0,8; Vox perdería 2,8 respecto a la macroencuesta y Frente Amplio bajaría un punto.

Respecto al barómetro de octubre, que tuvo una muestra de 5.025 entrevistas, el PSOE sube cuatro décimas y el PP 2,5 puntos, mientras que Vox cae 1,5 puntos y Frente Amplio 0,4, como puede consultarse en el siguiente gráfico.

El CIS elaboró la encuesta de este barómetro mediante 8.034 entrevistas telefónicas realizadas entre el 10 y el 17 de noviembre, con un margen de error de ±1,1% para el conjunto de la muestra. El trabajo de campo se realizó, pues, en plena campaña electoral, y contempla el accidente ferroviario de Urda y la posterior dimisión del ministro Óscar Puente y la huelga general del 11 de noviembre, pero se terminó antes del debate cara a cara televisado entre los candidatos del PSOE y el PP, Pedro Sánchez y Alberto Núñez Feijóo.

El CIS es la institución que realiza los sondeos más grandes de España, y es también la única de las principales casas encuestadoras, junto a SW Demoscopia (que realiza sondeos para la cadena de televisión La Séptima), que de forma regular pronostica que el PSOE será el partido más votado en las próximas elecciones generales y que la derecha formada por PP y Vox no alcanzará la mayoría absoluta.

Una estimación contraria a la del resto de sondeos, así como al promedio de DatosRTVE, calculado a partir del conjunto de encuestas publicadas, que señalan que el PP alcanzará la mayoría absoluta de manera holgada junto a Vox. Ninguna encuesta estima para los socialistas un porcentaje de voto tan alto ni uno tan bajo para los 'populares' como los que difunde el CIS.
sources.headline: El CIS estima que el PSOE ganar� las elecciones con casi diez puntos de ventaja sobre el PP

sources.body:
Pedro Sánchez Y Alberto Núñez Feijóo en el cara a cara

Las encuestas publicadas este lunes coinciden, todas menos la del Centro de Investigaciones Sociológicas (CIS), en situar como ganador a Alberto Núñez Feijóo y en otorgar al bloque PP y Vox una holgada mayoría absoluta que les permitiría gobernar tras las elecciones del próximo 29 de noviembre.

En el último día en el que la ley electoral permite la publicación de encuestas muchos medios han sacado sus últimos trackings coincidiendo con la publicación del barómetro de noviembre del CIS , que siguiendo la estela de los últimos meses da una ventaja de prácticamente 10 puntos del PSOE sobre el PP en voto estimado en una encuesta que no aporta atribución de escaños.

Los únicos medios que no descartan la victoria de Pedro Sánchez el próximo 29 de noviembre son los de Prisa y La Vanguardia. La encuesta de 40 dB para  El País y La Ser destaca que los socialistas se hallan a menos de un punto de los populares. No obstante, sostiene que PP y Vox mantienen una amplia mayoría absoluta que sitúa alrededor de los 187 escaños. La mayoría absoluta son 176 asientos en el Congreso.

La encuesta de estos medios sitúa el Partido Popular en primera posición con el 31,8 % de los votos y 130 escaños (incluidos dos de UPN-PP), pero el PSOE recorta distancias hasta situarse a apenas nueve décimas con el 30,9 % y 124 diputados. A pesar de este estrechamiento, la suma del bloque de la derecha mantiene una holgada mayoría absoluta de 187 escaños gracias al 17,3 % y 57 representantes de Vox.

Por su parte, el espacio a la izquierda de los socialistas queda relegado a 9 diputados en total (6 de Frente Amplio, que obtiene el 3,9 % en solitario, y 3 de Compromís-Front Valencià, mientras Podemos se queda sin representación.

Según el sondeo de Ipsos para  La Vanguardia publicado el domingo, el PP y el PSOE estarían separados por apenas medio punto en intención de voto, con un 30,3 % y 127 escaños (incluidos los de UPN) para los populares frente al 29,8% y 119 diputados para los socialistas. A pesar de este empate técnico en porcentaje de voto y de la ganancia de ocho escaños del PSOE respecto al anterior estudio, la suma del bloque de la derecha alcanzaría igualmente una cómoda mayoría absoluta de 190 escaños (14 por encima de los 176 necesarios) gracias al 17,9 % y 63 representantes de Vox. Por detrás, el espacio a la izquierda del PSOE se queda en 9 diputados en total —6 de Frente Amplio y 3 de Compromís—.

Ya lejos de estos datos, el último sondeo de Sigma Dos para  El Mundo  mantiene al PP en cabeza con el 31,7 % de los votos (124-130 escaños; 132 en la estimación central incluyendo UPN), seguido del PSOE con el 28,3 % (113-119 escaños) y Vox con el 17,9 % (58-63 escaños). Con estas cifras, la suma del bloque de la derecha alcanzaría los 190 diputados (en una horquilla de 182 a 193), holgadamente por encima de los 176, mientras que el espacio a la izquierda del PSOE queda muy fragmentado con Frente Amplio en el 7,2 % (11-14 escaños) y Podemos sin representación (0,7 %).

stories.headline: Plus Ultra suspends all flight operations while negotiating with SEPI

sources.body:
La aerolínea Plus Ultra ha anunciado el cese de sus actividades “hasta nuevo aviso” como “ejercicio de responsabilidad y prudencia” y tras “intensas negociaciones” para intentar mantener sus operaciones. El anuncio lo realizó unas horas después de dejar de vender billetes al único destino al que aún volaba, Venezuela. Deja ahora a su principal acreedor, la Sociedad Española de Participaciones Industriales (SEPI), en una situación comprometida y con una deuda de 53 millones de la que no ha recuperado nada del principal.

La empresa adopta esta medida tras solicitar hace unos días el preconcurso de acreedores e informar a los sindicatos de que prepara un expediente de regulación de empleo (ERE) para la plantilla, en un entorno de fuerte encarecimiento del queroseno por la guerra en Irán y problemas operativos.

Reconoce además en su web hallarse en una fase de “reestructuración financiera” en la que pugna por su “viabilidad a futuro”. Según dice, “actuará de conformidad con la normativa aplicable y con la debida consideración de los intereses de las personas afectadas”.

La ayuda recibida por la SEPI fue la primera de las destinadas a empresas estratégicas durante la pandemia y se ha convertido en la más controvertida. Se encuentra judicializada por el destino del dinero y por el esquema de comisiones para su obtención. El caso salpica al expresidente del gobierno José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero.

La compañía ofrece ahora vuelos en su web a los cinco destinos con los que ha venido operando, pero en el momento de contratarlos no es posible cerrar la operación. Las conexiones incluían Buenos Aires, Caracas, Lima, Bogotá y Cartagena de Indias.

Fuentes de la SEPI indican que el Fondo de Apoyo a la Solvencia de Empresas Estratégicas (FASEE) exige a la empresa “medidas que permitan garantizar la viabilidad y el mantenimiento de la actividad, que fue el objetivo” de la ayuda concendida.

El fondo, explican, “ha requerido a Plus Ultra soluciones concretas y viables para asegurar la continuidad de su actividad y la devolución de los fondos públicos recibidos”.

Según las últimas cuentas depositadas por Plus Ultra en el registro mercantil, su plantilla ronda las 600 personas y sus deudas ascienden, incluidos los 53 millones de euros de la SEPI, a 59 millones. Aquel ejercicio perdió 10 millones de euros.

Desde el entorno de la empresa aseguraron hace unos meses que el inicio de la investigación a Zapatero había bloqueado un proceso de venta a un inversor interesado.

Este plan de venta a un nuevo inversor fue uno de los mensajes transmitidos a la plantilla hace cerca de año por el propietario, Julio Martínez Sola. La idea era abordar una ampliación de capital para dar entrada a un inversor industrial, para lo que ya existían tres posibles interesados. Con ese dinero se devolvería la ayuda de la SEPI.

Sin un acuerdo con inversores interesados, la empresa inicia ahora unas negociaciones con los acreedores que, si se incluyen las prórrogas previstas en la legislación, le permite ganar seis meses de tiempo en busca de una solución.
sources.headline: Plus Ultra cesa sus actividades mientras negocia una solución con la SEPI

sources.body:
Avión de Plus Ultra. / PLUS ULTRA - Archivo

La aerolínea Plus Ultra ha decidido detener su actividad aérea y suspender todas sus operaciones desde este lunes y hasta nuevo aviso, incluidas las conexiones con Venezuela , su último destino regular después de los recortes aplicados durante las últimas semanas. La decisión llega en plena crisis financiera, con la compañía inmersa en un procedimiento preconcursal y mientras trata de negociar una salida con sus acreedores.

La empresa ha explicado en un comunicado que la suspensión responde a un ejercicio de "responsabilidad y prudencia" para gestionar la situación de forma ordenada, al tiempo que continúa evaluando las alternativas disponibles. También ha asegurado que actuará conforme a la normativa y teniendo en cuenta los intereses de las personas afectadas.

La compañía reconoce el impacto que la medida tendrá sobre sus distintos grupos de interés, desde los pasajeros y los empleados hasta sus proveedores. Según ha trasladado, los equipos correspondientes trabajarán para atender las solicitudes que se reciban. Por el momento, el comunicado no concreta cuándo podrían reanudarse los vuelos ni detalla las medidas previstas para los clientes con billetes ya adquiridos.

La situación tiene además implicaciones para las arcas públicas. Plus Ultra recibió en marzo de 2021 un apoyo financiero de 53 millones de euros de la Sociedad Estatal de Participaciones Industriales (SEPI) , a través del fondo habilitado durante la pandemia para respaldar a empresas estratégicas. La financiación se articuló mediante un préstamo ordinario de 19 millones y otro participativo de 34 millones. Este rescate público está siendo investigado en la Audiencia Nacional en el marco de la causa abierta contra el expresidente del Gobierno José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero y los directivos de Plus Ultra.

El anuncio supone un nuevo paso en el deterioro de la actividad de Plus Ultra. La aerolínea ya había comenzado a reducir su programación durante noviembre. Primero dejó de operar algunas conexiones con Latinoamérica y, el pasado 17 de noviembre, suspendió sus vuelos regulares a Argentina y Perú , mientras mantenía los enlaces con Venezuela. Colombia también figuraba entre las rutas que habían dejado de operar.

La conexión venezolana era, por tanto, la última que permanecía activa dentro de su red regular. La compañía, especializada en vuelos de largo recorrido entre España y Latinoamérica, había ido concentrando progresivamente su actividad ante las dificultades para sostener su estructura de costes.

El encarecimiento del combustible es uno de los factores que han agravado la situación. Según los datos trasladados por la dirección de la aerolínea, el gasto previsto en carburante para 2026 ha pasado de 69,13 millones de euros a 104,83 millones, un incremento del 51,6%. A ello se suma un resultado operativo negativo de 31,08 millones de euros entre febrero y agosto.

La suspensión llega después de que Plus Ultra comunicara el inicio de un proceso de negociación con sus acreedores a través de la vía preconcursal. Este mecanismo permite a una empresa en dificultades financieras ganar margen para intentar alcanzar un acuerdo con sus acreedores y evitar, si es posible, la declaración de concurso.
sources.headline: La aerolínea Plus Ultra suspende todas sus operaciones desde este mismo lunes

stories.headline: Supreme Court grants Puigdemont amnesty and closes the Catalan independence case

sources.body:
El Tribunal Supremo ha declarado la extinción de la eventual responsabilidad penal por amnistía del expresidente de la Generalitat catalana Carles Puigdemont y de los exconsellers Antoni Comín y Lluís Puig, así como el sobreseimiento libre de los hechos en la causa del ‘procés’.

El tribunal confirma el auto de conclusión de sumario dictado por el magistrado instructor, Pablo Llarena, el pasado 3 de noviembre.

En el auto, la Sala rechaza la pretensión planteada por el partido político Vox, que ejerce la acusación popular, que planteaba la suspensión de la aplicación de la amnistía a Puigdemont hasta que el Tribunal de Justicia de la Unión Europea resuelva una cuestión prejudicial planteada por el Tribunal Superior de Justicia de Catalunya.

Alternativamente, Vox proponía a la Sala la conveniencia de plantear una cuestión de prejudicialidad ante el tribunal europeo por el delito de malversación de caudales públicos.

Ambas pretensiones, dice el Supremo, la de suspensión y la del planteamiento de la cuestión prejudicial, se desestiman.

Para la Sala, la lectura de la sentencia del Tribunal de Justicia de la Unión Europea de 16 de julio del 2026 en relación con la ley de Amnistía “no evidencia las dudas que la acusación popular plantea, sin ninguna argumentación que respalde la pretensión deducida, que no son compartidas por esta Sala”.

Por tanto, no se estima necesaria una decisión del Tribunal de Justicia de la Unión Europea para aplicar ya la amnistía a Puigdemont.

Aunque, el juez instructor ya había dejado sin efecto el procesamiento contra él por la utilización de fondos públicos para organizar el referéndum del 1 de octubre del 2017, con esta decisión ya no hay vuelta atrás y el expresidente podrá abandonar Bélgica y volver a Catalunya ya sin causas pendientes.

En este caso, la Sala ha dictado un auto escueto simplemente aplicando la amnitía,y declarando el sobreseimiento libre de los hechos por extinción de la eventual responsabilidad penal por amnistía de Puigdemont, Toni Comin y Lluis Puig, cuyo procesamiento se dejó sin efecto en la misma resolución de conclusión del sumario.

Cuando el mes pasado amnistió a los líderes independentistas condenados, con Oriol Junqueras a la cabeza, el Supremo sí reprochó al Tribunal Constitucional el argumento que empleó para rechazar la psotura del alto tribunal de no aplicar la amnistía por el delito de malversación. Y apeló a que las consideraciones empleados fueron “manifiestamente prescindibles”.

Para los magistrados, atribuir a la interpretación de esta Sala para denegar la amistía una “drástica contradicción”, una “reducción teleológica”, una “interpretación extensiva”, una “interpretación impredecible de los preceptos aplicables”, un distanciamiento del “sentido común”, de “la lógica”, de la finalidad de la ley y, en fin, la ausencia de un elemental “nexo de coherencia”, tal y como recoge el TC en su sentencia, “representa enriquecer su decisión con consideraciones absolutamente innecesarias para el respaldo de lo resuelto”.

sources.body:
L'expresident Carles Puigdemont ha quedat definitivament amnistiat de la causa que fins fa uns dies encara seguia oberta al Suprem per l'organització del referèndum d'independència de l'1 d'octubre del 2017. L'amnistia i arxivament definitiu de la causa arriben en plena campanya electoral del 29N.

Juntament amb Puigdemont, la sala segona del tribunal també ha aplicat l'amnistia definitiva als exconsellers Lluís Puig i Toni Comín , que setmanes enrere ja van tornar de l'exili, tan bon punt el jutge Llarena va retirar les ordres de detenció .

L'últim que tornarà a casa des de l'exili belga serà l'expresident, que s'esperarà a fer el pas després de les eleccions espanyoles del 29N per preservar el caràcter institucional que vol donar al seu retorn.

Un cop s'ha anunciat l'aplicació definitiva de l'amnistia, Puigdemont ha publicat un missatge a la xarxa X amb un fragment del poema "El necessari naixement dels contrincants" del mallorquí Jaume Pons Alorda i ha dit que ha arribat el dia de recomanar-lo.

L'escrit, de manera irònica, va dirigit als " estimadíssims enemics " de l'autor, però en aquest cas s'entén que Puigdemont ho adreça al Tribunal Suprem. Destaca que és necessari que cada cop n'hi hagi més i "siguin millors i més esmolats" i els dona les gràcies "eternes" per donar-li raons per anar-los en contra.

Quan vaig llegir aquest poema d'en @jaumeponsalorda, del seu llibre "El Corc" (LaBreu Edicions), vaig pensar que un dia tindria l'ocasió per recomanar-lo. El dia ha arribat. (Compreu el llibre, per cert, que n'hi trobareu més i uns "deliciosos propòsits de procreació" finals que us ajudaran a gaudir-ne)

El pas definitiu del Suprem arriba dos anys i mig després de l'aprovació de l'amnistia al Congrés , un període marcat per les reticències dels tribunals a l'hora d'aplicar el text pactat entre els socialistes, Junts i ERC.

En el cas del Suprem, l'argument va ser que no podia aplicar l'amnistia en els casos associats a la malversació. Després que la justícia europea avalés el contingut de l'amnistia , també el relatiu a aquest punt, va ser el Constitucional qui va desencallar la situació.

Ho va fer el 6 d'octubre amb un pronunciament molt dur en què va ordenar amnistiar de manera immediata tots els membres del govern del 2017 que seguien en el punt de mira judicial.

A partir d'aquí, i a contracor, Llarena va aixecar les ordres de detenció, va tancar la causa i la va enviar a la sala segona del Suprem, que és la que ha arxivat definitivament el cas i ha aplicat l'amnistia a Puigdemont, Puig i Comín després de nou anys d'exili.

També fa un mes que van quedar amnistiats Junqueras i la resta d'exconsellers que encara no podien ocupar càrrecs públics, anys després d'haver sortit de la presó pels indults.

D'aquesta manera, tots els membres del govern independentista de l'octubre del 2017 estan amnistiats, tant els que van ser jutjats i condemnats com els que van marxar a l'exili.

Carles Puigdemont va aparèixer per sorpresa a Brussel·les acompanyat d'alguns dels consellers a finals d'octubre del 2017, hores després de la declaració d'independència.
